source.title: Insensitivity of Place Cells to the Value of Spatial Goals in a Two-Choice Flexible Navigation Task.

confidence_rationale: The most direct counter-evidence found: rats behaviorally preferred higher-value goals, yet dorsal CA1/CA3 place-cell activity was NOT modulated by goal value. The authors explicitly argue place cells form a 'value-free map' that links to value 'in other parts of the brain' -- i.e., value is applied downstream, the exact alternative MECH-073 denies. High confidence as a genuine conflict source; this is why the backlog flags MECH-073 active_conflict.
failure_signatures: Place-cell firing showed goal-related out-of-field activity but no value modulation; value affected behavior without a corresponding hippocampal value signal, directly instantiating a 'value-free spatial map + downstream value' architecture.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Dorsal hippocampal place cells encode space independently of its associated value; they form a spontaneously constructed value-free map that links to value-related information located elsewhere in the brain.
mapping.ree_translation: Weakens MECH-073: if the biological hippocampal map is value-free and valence is supplied by downstream structures (e.g. ventral striatum), then the REE claim that valence is INTRINSIC to hippocampal map geometry is contradicted for the dorsal-CA1 spatial code.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Scope caveat cuts toward reconciliation: this is DORSAL hippocampus and value = external reward magnitude at a goal. MECH-073 (via ARC-007/MECH-035) may concern a broader or more ventral/affective valence woven into map geometry, which this task does not probe. The weakening is strong for the dorsal-spatial-value case but does not necessarily refute an intrinsic-valence claim scoped to affective/ventral maps.
mapping.source_context: Rat dorsal CA1 and CA3 recordings; continuous place-navigation task dissociating spatial goal from reward consumption, two goals of differing reward magnitude.

confidence_components.notes: Well-controlled dissociation of goal from reward; high-quality direct counter-evidence. Mapping fidelity slightly reduced by the dorsal/external-reward scoping that leaves an affective-valence escape hatch.
